captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 6. In this lesson: A life in science.
Read a biography and use time connectives to follow events.
Here are some new words. Biography. The story of a person's life written by someone else. Scientist.
A person who studies the natural world. Award. A prize for doing something well.
And some more words. Discovery. Finding something for the first time. Education.
The learning you get at school and university. Inspire. Make someone want to do something great.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: the story of a person's life written by someone else?
Now some grammar: Time connectives in biographies. Biographies follow time order.
Use connectives like in 1950, as a child, later, after that, by the age of, eventually.
For example: As a child, she loved stars. For example: By the age of 20, she had finished university.
Now listen, and read along. Dr Asha Rao, the seed saver.
Asha Rao was born in a farming village in India in 1952.
As a child, she helped her grandmother collect seeds from the best rice plants every harvest.
Although few girls in her village went to university, Asha won a place to study plant science.
After that, she worked in labs in India and Brazil. In the 1980s,
Asha noticed that many old types of rice were disappearing because farmers were all planting the same new kind.
She decided to act.
Over the next thirty years, she and her team travelled to more than two hundred villages.
They collected and saved seeds from over 1,500 kinds of rice.
In 2015, Dr Rao received an international award. She said, ‘My grandmother was my first teacher.
She taught me that every seed is a story.’
Another question. The video will stop. Where was Asha Rao born?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like biography, scientist, award.
You practised time connectives in biographies. And you read Dr Asha Rao, the seed saver.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 6. In this lesson: Made and used.
Use the past simple passive to talk about inventions and history.
Here are some new words. Prototype. The first model of a new invention. Patent.
A document that says an invention belongs to you. Engineer.
A person who designs machines, roads or bridges.
And some more words. Manufacture. Make things in large numbers in a factory. Launch.
Send out or start something new. Wheelchair. A chair with wheels for people who cannot walk easily.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: the first model of a new invention?
Now some grammar: Past simple passive.
Use was, were + past participle when the person who did the action is less important or unknown.
Use ‘by’ to say who did it. For example: The bridge was built in 1932.
For example: The first phones were made by hand.
For example: The vaccine was developed by a team of doctors.
Now listen, and read along. The all-terrain wheelchair.
Ordinary wheelchairs work well on smooth floors, but sand, mud and rocks can stop them completely.
In 2008, a group of engineering students wanted to change this.
A first prototype was built from bicycle parts in a university workshop.
It was tested on a beach, where its wide tyres rolled easily over the sand.
The design was improved many times.
Lighter materials were used, and a hand-pedal system was added so users could climb small hills.
In 2012, a patent was given to the team, and the chair was manufactured by a small company.
Today, thousands of these chairs are used around the world, from mountain paths to national parks.
Another question. The video will stop. What can stop ordinary wheelchairs?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like prototype, patent, engineer.
You practised past simple passive. And you read The all-terrain wheelchair.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
